mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.1% signals accommodative monetary policy that compresses equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods with FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 3.0%, it triggers monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates and reduces valuation multiples, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS > 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals robust economic expansion, elevating corporate earnings expectations and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where both GDPC1 and HOUST show positive momentum (e.g., > 0.5% quarterly growth and > 1% monthly growth).

mechanism_narrative: High unemployment (UNRATE > 5.0%) indicates recession risk that suppresses corporate earnings growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where UNRATE > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) above 95.0 signals strengthening manufacturing activity, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days due to improved earnings momentum.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where INDPRO > 95.0.

mechanism_narrative: CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 250.0 indicates accelerating price pressures that may trigger central bank tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods where CPIAUCSL > 250.0.

mechanism_narrative: Retail sales (RSAFS) above 480,000 million dollars signals strong consumer spending, which typically drives positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days through elevated earnings growth expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where RSAFS > 480000.0.

mechanism_narrative: Payroll employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 137,000 thousand indicates a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where PAYEMS > 137000.0.
